content: Enalapril maleate and hydrochlorothiazide are combined in a medication used to treat hypertension. Enalapril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor, while hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic. This combination is FDA-approved for managing high blood pressure. The medication is marketed under the brand name Vaseretic®. Black Box Warning This drug carries a black box warning due to potential risks, including severe adverse reactions. It is essential to follow prescribing guidelines and monitor patients closely. Common Adverse Reactions The most frequently reported side effects include dizziness, headache, fatigue, and cough. These reactions are generally mild and transient. Adult Dosage For enalapril, the recommended dosage ranges from 10 to 40 mg per day, administered either once daily or in two divided doses. The maximum daily dose should not exceed 20 mg. Combination therapy with enalapril and hydrochlorothiazide is typically initiated only after monotherapy has failed to achieve the desired effect. The daily dosage of Vaseretic should not exceed two tablets. Pediatric Use There is no FDA-approved information regarding the use of enalapril maleate/hydrochlorothiazide in pediatric patients. Contraindications Vaseretic is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to any of its components, a history of angioedema related to ACE inhibitors, or hereditary/idiopathic angioedema. Due to the hydrochlorothiazide component, it is also contraindicated in patients with anuria or hypersensitivity to sulfonamide-derived drugs. Additionally, it should not be co-administered with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Warnings Hypotension Excessive hypotension is rare in uncomplicated hypertensive patients but may occur in those with severe salt or volume depletion, such as patients on diuretics or dialysis. Hypotension may also occur in patients with severe congestive heart failure or renal insufficiency. Therapy should be initiated under close medical supervision, especially in high-risk patients. Angioedema Angioedema involving the face, extremities, lips, tongue, glottis, or larynx has been reported with ACE inhibitors, including enalapril. This can occur at any time during treatment. If angioedema occurs, Vaseretic should be discontinued immediately, and appropriate therapy should be initiated. Laryngeal edema can be fatal and requires emergency intervention to secure the airway. Intestinal Angioedema Intestinal angioedema has been reported in patients treated with ACE inhibitors. Symptoms include abdominal pain, with or without nausea or vomiting. Diagnosis may require imaging or surgical exploration. Symptoms typically resolve after discontinuation of the ACE inhibitor. Neutropenia/Agranulocytosis ACE inhibitors, such as captopril, have been associated with neutropenia and agranulocytosis, particularly in patients with renal impairment or collagen vascular disease. While data for enalapril are insufficient, periodic monitoring of white blood cell counts is recommended in high-risk patients. Hepatic Failure Rarely, ACE inhibitors have been associated with a syndrome beginning with cholestatic jaundice and progressing to fulminant hepatic necrosis, sometimes resulting in death. Patients developing jaundice or significant elevations in hepatic enzymes should discontinue the drug and receive appropriate medical follow-up. Hydrochlorothiazide-Specific Warnings Thiazides should be used cautiously in patients with severe renal or hepatic disease. They may precipitate azotemia or hepatic coma in susceptible individuals. Thiazides can also cause electrolyte imbalances, including hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and hypochloremic alkalosis. Patients should be monitored for signs of fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Drug Interactions Enalapril Maleate Dual Renin-Angiotensin System Blockade: Combining ACE inhibitors with angiotensin receptor blockers or aliskiren increases the risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal dysfunction. Avoid co-administration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes or renal impairment. Diuretics: Patients on diuretics may experience excessive blood pressure reduction when starting enalapril. Adjustments to diuretic therapy or salt intake may be necessary. NSAIDs: Co-administration with NSAIDs may impair renal function and reduce the antihypertensive effect of enalapril. Monitor renal function periodically. Potassium-Sparing Agents: Concomitant use with potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, or potassium-containing salt substitutes may lead to hyperkalemia. Use with caution and monitor serum potassium levels. Lithium: ACE inhibitors can increase lithium levels, leading to toxicity. Monitor lithium levels closely if co-administered. Gold Therapy: Rare nitritoid reactions (e.g., facial flushing, nausea, hypotension) have been reported in patients receiving injectable gold and ACE inhibitors. Hydrochlorothiazide Alcohol, Barbiturates, Narcotics: May potentiate orthostatic hypotension. Antidiabetic Drugs: Dosage adjustments may be required due to altered glucose tolerance. Cholestyramine and Colestipol: These resins impair hydrochlorothiazide absorption, reducing its efficacy. Corticosteroids and ACTH: May exacerbate electrolyte depletion, particularly hypokalemia. Lithium: Thiazides reduce lithium clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity. Avoid concurrent use. Adverse Reactions Vaseretic has been evaluated in over 1,500 patients, with adverse reactions generally mild and transient. Common side effects include dizziness, headache, fatigue, and cough. Rare but serious reactions include angioedema, neutropenia, and hepatic failure. Hydrochlorothiazide-specific reactions include electrolyte imbalances, hyperuricemia, and photosensitivity. Monitoring Patients on Vaseretic should undergo regular monitoring of blood pressure, renal function, and serum electrolytes. Those with pre-existing renal or hepatic impairment require close observation.
